title: Jeep’s Wrangler Scrambler SRT Concept Boasts Backward-Facing Seats

body_markdown:
It’s no secret that Jeep is working on a flagship model called the Wrangler Scrambler. The off-roader has previously been[included in presentations](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/stellantis-new-model-pipeline-srt-jeep-dodge-ram/) , and executives have released several tidbits of information about it over the past couple of months. The new Jeep Wrangler Scrambler SRT Concept unveiled at SEMA 2026 gives us our best look yet at the upcoming range-topping desert truck.


The concept is based on[the Wrangler](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/the-2027-wrangler-jl-2a-harkens-back-to-jeeps-first-civilian-focused-model/) , but it shares little more than a name with its regular-production sibling. Jeep and SRT made hundreds of changes to turn the Wrangler into a high-speed off-roader that can keep up with[a Bronco Raptor](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2022-bronco-raptor-revealed/) through the desert.


The changes start with the styling, which is more truck-like than SUV-like. The Scrambler keeps the round headlights but wears a shorter, more angular version of Jeep’s seven-slot grille. While Jeep notes that the design is inspired by[the CJ-8 Scrambler](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/1981-86-jeep-cj-8-scrambler-smokin-hot/) , we also see a subtle resemblance between the concept and the SJ-generation Gladiator. The doors are longer than a Wrangler’s, and there’s a removable roof panel for open-air driving. Out back, a Scrambler-branded tailgate provides access to the rear compartment.

What you can put in the back depends on how it’s configured. These images show a rear-facing, two-person bench seat that reminds us of the[Subaru Brat](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/valuation/the-1978-93-subaru-brat-is-fun-functional-and-climbing/) . The seats are clipped into floor-mounted hooks, and a structural roll cage protects the whole cabin, so riding in the back won’t be as scary as it sounds. The seats can also be rotated to face the front, or removed entirely to create a storage compartment large enough to haul motorcycles. Spray-in bedliner should keep the back clean regardless of what’s in it.


Jeep hasn’t revealed what the concept is powered by, but we’d be surprised if there were fewer than eight cylinders under the vented hood. The brand had a lot to say about the suspension system, however. There’s a concept-specific, high-travel independent front suspension designed jointly with off-road racing champion Casey Currie and a[trophy truck](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorsports/peek-under-the-skin-of-a-spec-trophy-truck-and-discover-off-road-ingenuity/) –inspired rear axle. This is the first time that an independent front suspension has been fitted to the Wrangler; the model has used a solid front axle since its inception.


This layout was selected to improve steering precision, wheel control, and high-speed stability on rough terrain, according to Jeep. It’s complemented by what the company refers to as desert racing-style suspension hardware, including Fox shocks. While we’re talking about a concept, the basic suspension layout has already proven its mettle: It’s related to the system that was fitted to the Striker Concept unveiled earlier in 2026. Currie drove the Striker to a first-in-class finish during this year’s NORRA 500 race.


We’ve gotten used to seeing cool, wild concepts from Jeep, especially at[the annual Easter Safari](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/handful-of-killer-concepts-headline-easter-jeep-safaris-60th-anniversary/) , but most remain at the prototype stage. We’re betting that the Jeep Wrangler Scrambler SRT Concept is different. Jeep wants to give the Bronco Raptor a run for its money, so this SRT-branded, Wrangler-based truck/SUV mash-up is probably headed to a showroom near you in the coming years.
